ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the quadrilateral OABC is a square. An equilateral triangle $\triangle ABD$ is constructed with AB as the side, and point D is precisely on the x-axis. The diagonal CA intersects the x-axis at point E. If the coordinate of point E is $\left(4, 0\right)$, write down directly the degree measure of $\angle BDO$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows that in a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, the x-axis is horizontal to the right, D is located on the positive direction of the x-axis, and E is also on the x-axis and is between O and D; A is located below the x-axis, B is located to the upper right of A, and C is located to the upper right of O. Quadrilateral OABC is a tilted square, and line segment CA is its diagonal and intersects the x-axis at E. Construct equilateral triangle ABD with AB as a side to the right side; it can be seen in the figure that D is on the x-axis. Reasoning: Because OABC is a square, OA = AB, and ∠OAB = 90°. Because △ABD is an equilateral triangle, AB = AD, and ∠BAD = 60°. From OA = AB and AB = AD, obtain OA = AD; therefore △OAD is an isosceles triangle. According to the order of the rays at point A in the figure, ∠OAD = ∠OAB + ∠BAD = 90° + 60° = 150°. Therefore the two base angles of △OAD are equal, ∠ODA = ∠AOD = (180° − 150°)/2 = 15°. Also because △ABD is an equilateral triangle, ∠BDA = 60°. At point D, ray DO is located between DB and DA, so ∠BDO = ∠BDA − ∠ODA = 60° − 15° = 45°.
